clue.text: Match official sheltering companion in heat wave

indicators.note: the match official's word shelters, or holds inside it, the companion

parts.note: a scorer is an official who keeps the score of a match
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A referee shields a teammate during a spell of blistering weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorcher is informal for a blazing hot day, the sort a hot spell brings.

clue.text: Driver overseas encountered skirmish in estate

indicators.note: in puts the skirmish inside the estate

parts.note: an estate is a car, an estate car
a melee is a confused scuffle or skirmish

explanation.surface: A motorist abroad met a scuffle on a country estate.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British term for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameleer drives camels, in desert lands abroad.

clue.text: Going on foot was tedious, it's said — step on to vintage car

parts.note: running is going quickly on foot

indicators.note: it's said marks a word sounding like another

parts.note: bored is how one felt when something was tedious

explanation.surface: Travelling on foot was dull, so hop aboard an old car.
explanation.definitionFit: A running board is the footboard along the side of old cars.

clue.text: Given a hearing, an American novelist may …

indicators.note: given a hearing marks the novelist's name as heard aloud

parts.note: Nathaniel Hawthorne wrote The Scarlet Letter

explanation.surface: Listen to an American writer, who might go on to say more.
explanation.walkthrough: May reads as a verb but is the definition: may is another name for the hawthorn tree or its blossom.
explanation.definitionFit: May is a common name for the hawthorn tree, which blossoms in that month.

clue.text: … rave about a girl glowing with happiness

indicators.note: the rave word goes about the others

parts.note: to rant is to rave
Di is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Ranting about a girl beaming with joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiant describes a face shining with joy or happiness.

clue.text: Coach beginning to refine an old actor

parts.note: a stage is a stagecoach

indicators.note: beginning to says take the first letter

explanation.surface: A trainer starts polishing an elderly performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stager is an archaic word for a player, an actor of the stage.

clue.text: Fine judge visiting islands — lots of them!

definitions.text: Fine judge visiting islands — lots of them!

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: the judge visits, goes inside, the islands

parts.note: I is short for island, so islands are two I's

explanation.surface: A good judge tours a nation of many islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiji is an archipelago nation of over three hundred islands.

clue.text: Polish member entering spiritualists' meeting after the start

indicators.note: entering puts the member inside the meeting word
after the start means the meeting word loses its first letter

parts.note: a seance is a meeting to contact spirits
a leg is a limb, a member

explanation.surface: A Polish limb gatecrashes a seance.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish here is refinement, poise, the noun sense of grace and style.

clue.text: A right pain crossing Mile End, like the bloody tube!

indicators.note: the nuisance word lies across, so encloses, the letter that follows

parts.note: a trial is a pain, a trying nuisance

indicators.note: Mile End is read as the end letter of the word Mile

explanation.surface: A grumble about the Tube line through Mile End, the London Underground station, being a bloody nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Mile End looks like the London station but gives only its last letter, E, which goes inside TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An artery is a tube carrying blood, so arterial describes such a blood vessel.

clue.text: Old soldiers writing on the wall

parts.note: men is a common word for soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Graffiti left on a wall by veterans of the army.
explanation.definitionFit: The writing on the wall is an idiom for a sign of doom to come, which is a portent.

clue.text: Studying cipher primarily? No way

indicators.note: primarily says the word for cipher comes first, before the word for studying

parts.note: a cipher is a zero, nothing
doing a subject means studying it, as in doing French

explanation.surface: Someone asked if they study codes mainly gives a flat refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms of blunt refusal, meaning certainly not.

clue.text: Main expert somehow got cool in sea

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are worked into another order

explanation.surface: A marine scientist somehow got cold in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Main is the sea, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: An oceanologist studies the oceans; the main is a poetic word for the sea.

clue.text: Unprofitable books about building

parts.note: a lean year is a thin, unprofitable one

indicators.note: about turns the books abbreviation round

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the crossword's usual books

explanation.surface: Accounts of a structure that never made money.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed or building propped against a wall.

clue.text: Scandinavian opera about singular English knight

indicators.note: the opera's name goes about, round, the next two letters

parts.note: Norma is an opera by Bellini
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A Nordic opera about a lone English knight.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norseman is a man of ancient Scandinavia, a Viking.

clue.text: It may identify a group of military musicians

parts.note: RM is the Royal Marines, a British military force
a band is a group of musicians, so musicians here stands for band

explanation.surface: A badge that picks out a regimental band.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a definition of a military band; in fact 'It may identify' is the definition, as stewards and captains wear one.
explanation.definitionFit: An armband is a strip worn on the sleeve to mark the wearer's role, like a captain or steward.

clue.text: The French came up with material to clothe a countryman of theirs

indicators.note: in a down clue came up turns the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: la is French for the

indicators.note: the material clothes, surrounds, the letter

parts.note: satin is a material

explanation.surface: French people produced fabric to dress a compatriot.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alsatian comes from Alsace, a region of France, so a fellow countryman of the French.

clue.text: Run round with instrument for beating flax

indicators.note: the run word goes round the short form of with

parts.note: a single is one run in cricket

explanation.surface: A dash round the field carrying a flax-beating tool.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a single is a run scored by one dash between the wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: A swingle is a wooden blade used to beat and clean flax fibres.

clue.text: City girl supporting pub Mayfair

clue.text: See work complete, rejecting wife's opening.

parts.note: lo is an old word for see, look
op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: rejecting says the complete word throws out the letter for wife

parts.note: whole means complete

explanation.surface: Watch the job finished, minus the wife's first move.
explanation.definitionFit: A loophole is a small opening, as in a slit in a wall.

clue.text: In holdall, keeping top of tea caddy

indicators.note: keeping means the bag holds the others inside

parts.note: a bag is a holdall

indicators.note: top of in a down clue means the first letter

parts.note: a tea caddy is a tin

explanation.surface: Inside a holdall, holding the lid of a tea caddy.
explanation.walkthrough: In is the definition: a cricketer who is in is batting.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a player who is in is currently batting.

clue.text: Single issue, a woman's work

parts.note: a son is a child, issue, here a single one
Tina is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A one-off edition of a magazine as one woman's effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonatina is a short sonata, a musical work.

clue.text: Popular crew reportedly instinctive …

indicators.note: reportedly marks words heard aloud

parts.note: in means popular and an eight is a rowing crew

explanation.surface: A well-liked rowing team said to act by gut feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Innate means inborn, instinctive rather than learnt.

clue.text: Both ends of leggings tucked into sort of light grip

indicators.note: those letters are tucked inside the light word

parts.note: neon is a kind of light, as in neon signs

indicators.note: both ends of a word gives its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Tights tucked under a lamp give a firm hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A nelson is a wrestling hold, a grip applied from behind the opponent.

clue.text: Not heed strange obsession? It's normal behaviour

indicators.note: strange suggests the two words are made odd, rearranged

parts.note: a thing is an obsession, as in having a thing about

explanation.surface: Ignoring an odd fixation is just how things are done.
explanation.definitionFit: The done thing is the socially accepted way of behaving.

clue.text: … extremely eager to advance therefore

indicators.note: extremely means the word's outermost letters

parts.note: to go is to advance

explanation.surface: Very keen to push on, then.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, used in English logic.

clue.text: Piece of music once representing a saint?

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bit of old church music depicting a holy figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a religious image, often depicting a saint in Orthodox tradition.

clue.text: Pope, say, giving name to Georgian resort

parts.note: Augusta is a city in the US state of Georgia, home of the Masters golf

explanation.surface: The Pope lends his name to a holiday town in Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: Pope is not the pontiff but Alexander Pope, the poet; Georgian suggests Britain's Georgian era but means the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope is a chief poet of the Augustan age of English letters.

clue.text: Enterprising person's giant missive not opened

parts.note: Gog is a legendary giant, of Gog and Magog

indicators.note: not opened means the letter word loses its first letter

parts.note: a letter is a missive

explanation.surface: An ambitious type's giant letter lies unopened.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-getter is an ambitious, enterprising person who chases success.
